hypothesis_status: OVERTURNED (again -- the captain's own correction was also incomplete)
filed_hypothesis: Missing imported Win32 prototypes leave recovery dependent on local argument scoring.
captain_refutation: p4_calls input-trial scoring at a call whose argument register is defined in a dominating predecessor block.
decisions: NEITHER DIAGNOSIS SURVIVES MEASUREMENT. It is not missing Win32 prototypes (the captain already refuted that) and it is not predecessor-block argument scoring either. `--option calleedeadarg off` restores CloseHandle(v2) and Process32NextW(v2,v4) verbatim on the witness, so kuna's OWN dead-argument veto is deleting them; the ancestor/trial machinery the captain pointed at scores both trials ACTIVE and USED. Instrumented at check_input_trial_use: on the first pass every trial comes out realistic=true solid=true only=true, and on the post-restart pass the RCX trials arrive already marked no-use with no ancestor call at all -- the calleedeadarg arm short-circuits ahead of it.

ROOT CAUSE: CalleeEntryDead::proves_dead is vacuously true when the walk recorded no path terminator. The test is `cuts.iter().all(|c| range fully written in c)`, and `all()` over an empty Vec is true -- for every register at once. The walk ends with an empty cut list when every path is closed by the revisit rule (`prev.is_subset(&frame.written)` -> continue) instead of by a RETURN / nested call / undecodable instruction, and nothing else in the summary distinguishes that from a proof.

WHY A PE IMPORT LANDS THERE, measured: a PE import's FuncCallSpecs entry address is its IAT slot in .rdata, so the probe decodes a pointer as instructions. KeyCheker's kernel32 IAT holds hint/name RVAs 0x68d0/0x68e2/0x68f4, and the two that start 0xf4 (`hlt`, whose x86-64 p-code branches to itself) produce complete=true ncuts=0 -- CloseHandle (nreads=0) and Process32NextW (nreads=44). Process32FirstW's slot starts 0xe2 and produces one cut, which is the ONLY reason it kept both arguments in the same run.

THE VETO NEEDS A RESTART TO REACH AN IMPORT AT ALL. seed_callee_entry_dead runs after the flow build, where a `call [rip+..]` is still a CALLIND with no entry address; only the re-flow forced by the no-return discovery of `abort` seeds the resolved IAT entries. That is why the argument survives the first ActionActiveParam pass and dies on the second, and why the reduced fixture has to import and call `abort`.

FIXED IN proves_dead, NOT IN THE WALK. `complete` means 'covered every path with nothing abandoned', and on a closed loop that is accurate -- the walk really did finish. What is unsound is the claim built on it, so the guard belongs where the conjunction is. Keeping `complete` honest also keeps is_complete() usable for diagnostics.

NO OPTION, deliberately. AGENTS.md gates FEATURES behind a named option and exempts 'a strict bug fix that only corrects wrong output'. This can only ever make an existing option decline a veto it had no evidence for; a knob whose `off` position is a known-unsound rule would be worse than no knob. calleedeadarg's own `off` remains the escape hatch for the pass as a whole.

THE SECOND INSTANCE IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT AND IS NOT CLOSED. 68d9ee36 (VirtualAlloc losing 0x40 in R9D, crackme.exe sub_140004dcc) still prints VirtualAlloc(0,0x36,0x3000) after this fix, and prints the same with `--option calleedeadarg off` -- so it never went through this path. It is a trailing-register-argument loss and wants its own need.

THE ACCEPTANCE PROBE'S TARGET IS A DATASET BINARY, so --promote refuses it. tests/cli/win32-process-enumeration-loses.json keeps the acceptance's `expect` block VERBATIM (both stdout_matches and both stdout_absent clauses) against a 2560-byte PE32+ written byte by byte by calleedeadarg_noterm_x86_64.py: four kernel32 imports whose hint/name entries are pinned to RVAs ending 0xF4 so every IAT slot decodes `hlt` first, one no-return `abort` call to force the re-flow, and the handle in RCX from a dominating predecessor. It reproduces `Process32NextW()` / `CloseHandle()` before the fix and both argument lists after it.
